A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same distributional-RL regularization framework and DERAC algorithm despite substantial reframing. All 16 pages of v4 and 21 pages of v5, including their appendices, provide sufficient readable text, equations, tables, and figures for comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original Atari and continuous-control experiments, including density-decomposition tests, DERAC learning curves, and entropy ablations in Figures 2–6.

after.justification: v5 retains original experimental results and adds Atari evaluations, DERAC comparisons, and categorical entropy ablations, including Figures 7–8 in the appendices.

M1.justification: DERAC retains the combined squared TD-error and cross-entropy critic loss, actor objective, and Algorithm 1 updates. v4 already implements the bin-based decomposition in Section 4.1. v5's histogram formalization and revised coefficient parametrization change the theoretical derivation without establishing a change to the implemented procedure.

E1.justification: Figure 2 expands Atari coverage from the plotted Breakout, Seaquest, and Hero experiments to eight games, adding Alien, BattleZone, Frostbite, Gopher, and StarGunner. The continuous-control task set is retained: Humanoid and Walker2D already appeared in v4's IQN experiments, although v5 additionally evaluates DERAC on them.

E2.justification: v5 adds entropy-free categorical DAC(C51) as a comparator for DERAC in Figure 7. Also, the corresponding Hero panel in Figure 5 replaces v4's C51_CE comparison with epsilon-decomposed C51 variants. The principal DQN, C51, SAC, and IQN-based comparator sets otherwise remain.

E3.justification: Appendix N extends the entropy-interaction evaluation design to a 51-atom C51 critic alongside the retained IQN study. Appendix M introduces DERAC comparisons against entropy-free DAC(C51). Table 1's existing settings are unchanged; relabeling Atari axes from time steps to frames does not establish a changed training budget.

E4.justification: Appendix N adds systematic vanilla-entropy and distributional-regularization on/off comparisons using C51 across seven retained environments, testing whether the interaction previously studied with IQN also occurs in the categorical family. Existing decomposition and lambda-sensitivity analyses remain. The Hero cross-entropy-versus-KL check is no longer displayed in Figure 5.

E5.justification: The reporting practice remains three seeds for Atari and five for continuous-control experiments, with smoothing size five for the entropy-interaction plots. No new confidence-interval definition, significance test, or uncertainty-estimation procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: v5 adds results for five Atari games, DERAC on Humanoid and Walker2D, and seven C51 entropy-interaction evaluations. Figure 8 newly shows that adding vanilla entropy to categorical distributional AC can hurt Ant, HalfCheetah, and Swimmer while helping HumanoidStandup and Walker2D. Several earlier learning curves are retained; Figure 5 loses the Hero C51_CE result.

T1.justification: v4's continuous CDF/Dirac-mixture assumption and approximation bound are replaced by a histogram decomposition with the validity condition epsilon >= 1 - p_E. v5 adds categorical–histogram optimization equivalence, a uniform density-estimation bound, a formal link to fitted Q-iteration, and an interpolation-loss derivation. The earlier KL properties and policy-iteration proofs are largely retained under new numbering.

C1.justification: v4's broad explanation of distributional RL superiority through risk-sensitive regularization becomes an explicitly CDRL-centered explanation of potential benefits through distribution matching and uncertainty-aware exploration. The revised abstract, introduction, and conclusion change the central mechanism and calibrate the scope of the theoretical contribution.

C2.justification: v4 describes exploration toward returns with greater dispersion. v5 instead emphasizes actors seeking distribution mismatch and critics reducing it, potentially dispersing or concentrating their estimates. It also adds explicit qualifications about valid decomposition parameters, incomplete theoretical transfer beyond CDRL, and the simulator issue excluding BipedalWalkerHardcore from Appendix N.

D1.justification: Appendix M newly supplies state/action dimensions for Humanoid and Walker2D and explicitly identifies DAC(C51) as DSAC without policy entropy. The main implementation recipe, hyperparameter table, network-source attribution, and code-access information otherwise remain essentially unchanged.

R1.justification: The new Related Work section substantially revises positioning around Lyle et al. (2019), Rowland et al. (2023a), and Wu et al. (2023), distinguishing nonlinear approximation, asymptotic convergence, and predictive-error guarantees. This replaces the earlier emphasis on representation dynamics and Wasserstein gradient-flow explanations and accompanies expanded citations on optimization, robustness, and risk sensitivity.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, theoretical exposition, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. v5 introduces an explicit contribution list and Related Work section, separates value-based and actor-critic analyses into major sections, reorganizes the appendices, and systematically replaces risk-sensitive terminology with uncertainty-aware and distribution-matching language.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout. Figure 1 becomes a two-case illustration; Figure 2 becomes an eight-game Atari grid; retained continuous-control decomposition and DERAC plots are combined in Figure 3. v5 adds Figures 7–8, changes legends and axes, replaces the Hero panel in Figure 5, and relocates the hyperparameter table.

improvement.justification: The explicit finite-bin decomposition condition and clearer CDRL scope improve the alignment between theory and the studied algorithms, while the new C51 ablations strengthen empirical support. These gains are limited by errors in the added theory: Equation 32 mistakes an O(Delta) bound for o(Delta), and Equation 36 mishandles the squared-residual cross term. Figure 5 also loses the advertised Hero cross-entropy comparison.
